subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Lee <sophia.lee@novaretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Sophia (and Rajesh),

Thanks again for taking the time today — I appreciated the context on NovaRetail's roadmap and your key constraints. Below is a short recap from our call so we have aligned next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

High-level pain points you shared
- Rising per-token costs and vendor lock with current providers (OpenAI + Anthropic).
- Latency spikes during peak traffic (personalization pipelines) that impact conversion.
- Concern about API parity for tool-calling/function-calling and existing prompt engineering investments.
- Security/compliance requirements: SOC 2 evidence and VPC/private deployment options for PII flows.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Generation: OpenAI GPT-4.1 via hosted API for product descriptions and personalization.
- Safety/use-case buffering: Anthropic for content filters on certain flows.
- Serving: Custom Node.js service with in-house queuing and caching layer; batch size tuned to limit latency.
- Metrics: SLO: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), target cost reduction 30%+ when migrating.

Success criteria for a migration proof-of-concept (POC)
- Functional parity: model(s) must support streaming, instruction-following, and function/tool calling compatible with your current prompts.
- Latency: P95 <= 300ms for targeted persona prompts in our staging region.
- Cost: expected token cost (in production profile) at least 30% lower than current spend.
- Safety: comparable filtering/guardrails with auditability and hooks for your moderation pipeline.
- Compliance: ability to run in VPC/private deployment and provide SOC2 artifacts.

Compatibility needs we flagged
- Tokenization and prompt-format parity (so prompts don’t need major rework).
- Streaming & partial response support for UI UX parity.
- Deterministic function/tool-calling behavior (to avoid additional parsing layers).
- Quantization profiles for smaller CPU/GPU footprints if you want on-prem options.

Initial model shortlist (open / community models we discussed)
- Llama 2 / Meta family (13B and 70B variants) — strong instruction-following with ecosystem tool support.
- Mistral-Instruct 7B — good cost/latency tradeoff for shorter prompts.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct — high quality for instruction tasks, suitable if you need larger-context understanding.
- RedPajama-INCITE / Eleuther-like variants — useful for fine-tune parity and self-hosting.

Next steps (agreed on call)
1) Redwood to run a targeted benchmark on a subset of your prompts (we'll mirror a sampling of 10 prompts + function calls) — deliverables: latency/cost/quality matrix. (Action: Aditya, ETA 5 business days)
2) Share compatibility matrix & SOC2 summary (attached). (Action: Marissa)
3) If benchmarks look good, propose a 4-week POC (dedicated capacity + VPC option) with straightforward success criteria.
4) Internal alignment at NovaRetail: Rajesh to confirm PO/POC budget and timeline.

Attachments included
- redwood-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (mapping of API parity and feature support)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2 scope & evidence types)

If this looks right, I’ll kick off the benchmark and loop Aditya to schedule a short tech sync for next week.

Best,

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192


From: Sophia Lee <sophia.lee@novaretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@novaretail.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful and captures the conversation well. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

- Confirmed: our priority is reducing unit cost while keeping developer effort minimal. We can tolerate small changes to prompts but want to avoid a full rework.
- For the POC, we can provide a small dataset of 10 representative prompts (including 2 function-calling examples) and traffic profile for benchmarking.
- On compliance: SOC2 artifacts are a hard requirement for the POC (we have an internal checklist) — thanks for the summary PDF, I’ll pass it to security.
- Timeline: We’re good to start the benchmark next week. Rajesh will confirm budget and will loop in procurement if needed.

One question: can your benchmarking include both non-quantized and INT8 quantized runs where applicable? We want to see the latency/cost tradeoffs.

Appreciate it — please kick off the tech sync, and I’ll get the prompt samples over by Thursday.

Best,
Sophia
Head of Personalization | NovaRetail
sophia.lee@novaretail.com | (212) 555-0143
